title: Prejudice now versus the 1920s
summary: She thinks race relations are better, including seating on streetcars.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, Archie Bunker is a very prejudiced man. He's prejudiced against Negroes.

He sure is. (Unintelligible), but I think he's kind of prejudiced, but his son-in-law told him, "Why are you prejudiced against --" Ku Klux Klan and that told him. "I ain't no Ku Klux Klanner." "I --" "What you doing burning a cross out there ?" He said, "I don't --" Oh, he tried (unintelligible), but his son-in-law told him.
Do you think there's less prejudice in the world now than there was in the '20s?
You think there's just as much prejudice now against black people?
Oh, no, I think it's better.
Yeah, I think it's better. I think

white people are a little bit better to colored people than they used to be. Colored people kind of didn't -- like you find a lot of white people was trying to (unintelligible) because they say black is beautiful ______. It seemed to me black is all right. Some people trying to ______.
You think it's a lot better than in the '20s?

Yeah, I do. I know they treat you better on the streetcars. There used to be but one seat for colored, but now, they put the thing up as high as it going to get. As long as somebody ______, they move you up.
It would be easier to travel now than it was in those years, earlier years.
